heading: Tuesday, October 27, 2026
topLine: OpenAI and Anthropic each say their internal models independently refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis with a subexponential 3-SAT algorithm; OpenAI also claims Kakeya and QCD proofs, and none of it is independently verified yet.

items.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic both claim their AI models refuted the Exponential Time Hypothesis; OpenAI adds Kakeya and QCD proofs
items.summary: OpenAI says internal models found a subexponential-time 3-SAT algorithm (refuting ETH), proved local smoothing in every dimension (implying the Kakeya and Stein restriction conjectures), and proved 4D Yang–Mills/QCD exists. Hours later, Anthropic's Levent Alpöge posted a paper credited to Claude, "A 2^o(n) Time Algorithm for 3-SAT". He says an internal Claude research model found the core algorithm on October 16 with 14M output tokens and no human input. Each lab released a Lean formalization, and Anthropic's paper calls the two results independent and concurrent. The ETH authors Impagliazzo and Paturi, with Ryan Williams, will lead review of OpenAI's claim, and a panel led by David Gross has OpenAI's physics work. Nothing is peer-reviewed yet, and both labs describe the 3-SAT speedups as purely asymptotic, with no practical impact.

items.headline: AMD will put $1B into Meta's equity raise and widen their AI infrastructure partnership
items.summary: AMD said Tuesday it will invest $1 billion in the share offering that is part of Meta's plan to raise up to $95B for AI. It also expanded the partnership across EPYC CPUs, Instinct GPUs, Pensando networking and ROCm, and said Helios racks are now installed and being tested at Meta. Analysts called the stake small next to Meta's size, more a sign of alignment than of funding need, and raised fresh questions about circular financing.

items.headline: Opera proposes 'WebAI', a web standard for running open-weight models locally in the browser
items.summary: WebAI lets web pages run text generation, classification and similar tasks on the user's own device with open-weight models such as Gemma, or Apple's on-device foundation model on Macs, without a cloud round-trip. It is opt-in and ships as an early preview in Opera One, with Opera GX and Neon to follow. Other browser makers have not yet said whether they will support it.

items.headline: Desktop 'AI teammate' workspaces climb GitHub trending: Cindy and OpenBot
items.summary: Cindy (makecindy, Apache-2.0) is an open-source agent for desktop and mobile that drives your files, browser and apps, using Claude Code, Codex or Pi as its harness. It has 7.3k stars, about 1,450 of them today. OpenBot (nightly-labs) is a local-first workspace that runs persistent Codex, Claude and Grok agents, each with its own task queue and browser control, and lets them work together. It has 2.1k stars, about 800 today; it is a development preview and recently moved to a noncommercial license.

items.headline: Google DeepMind finds predictable scaling laws for reinforcement learning, using an Elo-style score
items.summary: Zheng, Lyle, Khetarpal and Dabney fit scaling laws for actor-critic RL on Starpilot and Craftax. The laws predict performance, compute allocation and the best hyperparameters for runs with up to about 100× more compute. The key is scoring agents with an Elo-style rating instead of noisy mean episode return. Scaling up on these predictions set a new state of the art on Craftax.

items.headline: RSI Arena: ten frontier models each post-trained a 30B base model on their own
items.summary: Each agent got six days, 1,000 GPU-hours and $300 of API credit to turn Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B Base into an assistant, and all ten produced working models. The best, trained by GPT-6 Astra, closed a median 76% of the gap to NVIDIA's own Instruct model. Feedback from user votes improved eight of the ten, but benchmark gains did not track human preference, and one model became more likely to comply with harmful requests. Authors include Thomas Wolf and Alex Pentland.

items.headline: Trial by Trace: the best-scoring coding agent isn't the most reliable harness
items.summary: TraceTrial-Bench scores the harness itself (Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek Harness, OpenClaw) on 95 tasks with 9 models. Claude Code had the highest task success (44%), but OpenClaw best met the harness reliability criteria. In 31% of runs the agent succeeded while breaking at least one harness rule, which outcome-only benchmarks miss. It is one of the most-upvoted papers on Hugging Face today.

items.headline: Cloudflare discloses cross-tenant KV cache exposure on its Workers AI GLM-5.3 endpoint
items.summary: From August 27, the endpoint advertised a ~1M-token context, but its prefill KV cache held only 681K tokens. That misconfiguration plus an SGLang bug could leak cache data between customers on very long prompts. A researcher reported it on September 8, and Cloudflare pulled the model and fixed it. HN commenters praised the candor and criticized shipping with a known capacity mismatch.

items.headline: General Compute raises $100M Series A for GPU-free inference clouds
items.summary: Blackbird Ventures and Abstract Ventures led the round, valuing the startup at $800M post-money, up from $60M at its May seed. General Compute builds bare-metal inference capacity from non-Nvidia chips, including a $400M SambaNova order plus Cerebras and Positron hardware, often in converted bitcoin-mining sites. It targets 75 MW in 2027, a bet against the souring 'neocloud' sentiment.
